Hi Jenna / Tom —

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Quick recap and next steps related to the data handling items you raised so we have a clear record: 

1) Telemetry & logging: you asked whether telemetry sent to our monitoring vendors includes any user PII. Short answer: no — telemetry we send is metric/usage level and request identifiers (hashed) only. We do not send raw customer content to telemetry providers unless explicitly permitted in a signed agreement.

2) Data retention / logs: default retention for request logs is 90 days. We offer configurable retention windows down to 7 days for enterprise plans; we can discuss a custom retention schedule if needed.

3) Data residency / cloud regions: Redwood hosts customer inference workloads in specific cloud regions (e.g., us-east-1, us-west-2). For dedicated/private deployments we can ensure all inference and ephemeral storage remains in the contracted region.

4) Third-party subprocessors & marketplace flows: I attached our current subprocessors summary (redwood_subprocessors_summary.pdf). This includes telemetry vendors, cloud providers (AWS, GCP), and marketplace distribution partners.

Next steps we proposed on the call:
- Jenna: share the Acme security questionnaire sections on telemetry and retention (you mentioned a short form) — we can populate and return by EOD Monday.
- Redwood: loop in Security (Neha) and Product (Priyom) to confirm technical controls + provide any relevant diagrams (telemetry flow, marketplace flow).
- Schedule follow-up call with Acme security team.

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_summary.pdf (summary of subprocessors + high-level controls)

Subject: Re: Acme Health — telemetry, retention, and marketplace flow (answers)

Hi all —

Thanks for raising these — below are concise answers we can share with Acme. Happy to expand or hop on a call with your security team.

1) PHI/PII in telemetry: Redwood does not send customer PHI/PII to telemetry vendors. Telemetry we forward is aggregate metrics, service-level logs, and hashed request identifiers. We explicitly strip request payloads and do not include customer-provided content or health identifiers.

2) Hashing & KMS: Request identifiers are hashed using SHA-256. For Private/Dedicated deployments customers can opt to use their own KMS (customer-managed CMKs) for additional key separation. For hosted customers we manage keys in a hardened KMS (AWS KMS) with strict access controls.

3) Retention windows: default request/log retention is 90 days. For enterprise customers we offer contractual retention reductions (e.g., 30/14/7 days) and automatic deletion flows. Logs required for billing/usage metering are retained for up to 1 year but can be scoped by contract.

4) Marketplace flows (AWS Marketplace): Usage metering for Marketplace billing is limited to aggregated usage metrics (SKU-level) and does not include customer-identifiable content. No raw request payloads are sent to the marketplace partner. We have an architecture diagram documenting the flow (I’ll attach the redwood_telemetry_flow.png in the follow-up).

5) Compliance artifacts: SOC 2 Type II and our security pack are available — I’ll share a link to the security portal. If Acme needs an IP-protected NDA view, we can arrange an on-demand SOC2 review through our compliance portal.

Next steps: I can join a 30-min sync with Acme security to walk through the flow and KMS options. If you want, I’ll draft a short one-page response to Jenna’s questionnaire for quick review.

-Neha
Director of Security, Redwood Inference
